0.0.n: 今 combines with シーズン to specify the current sports season.

0.1.n: 勝 counts wins, and 目 marks their order: this is win number six.

0.3.n: This is the pitcher's name, written in katakana.

0.4.n: After ニール, this identifies his baseball position and serves as a title.

0.5.n: This polite ending completes the introduction of Neal.

0.7.n: Adding ございます makes this congratulatory expression polite.

0.8.n: ござい is part of ございます; here it adds politeness rather than a separate literal meaning.

0.9.n: ます completes ございます, making the congratulatory phrase respectful.

1.0.n: This drawn-out sound gives the speaker a moment to begin his reply.

1.2.n: Adding ございます makes this expression of gratitude more polite.

1.3.n: ござい is part of ございます, which makes ありがとう more respectful.

1.4.n: ます completes ございます in this standard polite expression of gratitude.

2.0.n: This English-based expression praises the pitcher's performance.

2.1.n: でし is the portion of でした that comes before the past ending た.

2.2.n: た completes でした, the past form of polite です, referring to the finished performance.

3.0.n: あざ is the first part of あざっす, a very casual shortening of ありがとうございます.

3.1.n: っす finishes the slang expression あざっす; the whole phrase is much less formal than ありがとうございます.

4.0.n: Adding ございます makes this congratulatory expression polite.

4.1.n: ござい is part of ございます; here it adds politeness rather than a separate literal meaning.

4.2.n: ます completes ございます, making the congratulatory phrase respectful.

5.0.n: あざー stretches the first part of あざっす, a very casual shortening of ありがとうございます.

5.1.n: っす finishes this stretched-out slang expression of gratitude, rather than forming a separate word here.

0.lit: This season, sixth win; it is pitcher Neal. Congratulations!
0.tip: 目 after a win count makes it an ordered milestone: ６勝目 is the sixth win.

1.tip: ありがとうございます is the standard polite way to express gratitude.

2.tip: でした is the polite past form of です, so the praise refers to a completed performance.

3.tip: あざっす compresses ありがとうございます into very casual speech, best avoided in formal situations.

4.tip: ございます makes おめでとう polite; it does not add a separate literal idea here.

5.tip: The ー shows a stretched vowel, giving this casual expression a drawn-out delivery.
